Avant d’entrer dans la méthode, il faut: Before entering the method, you must speak the same language as the staff. Flip each card to check the definition, then move on to the test.
Ce qui est reconnu comme certain, incont: What is recognised as certain and indisputable (objective in nature).
Raisonnement partant de l’observation d’: Reasoning that starts from the observation of a fact.
Conséquence ou jugement déduit d’une déd: Consequence or judgement drawn from a deduction (subjective in nature). Takes the form of tasks, constraints, imperatives, requests, intelligence requirements or amendments to the timeline.
Les modes d’action amis (MA) sont compar: Friendly courses of action (MA) are compared with one another against criteria (weighted or not) set or approved by the commander, in order to draw their relative advantages and disadvantages.
Opposer chaque MA à chaque mode d’action: Pit each MA against each enemy course of action (ME), by successive phases or time steps, checking that each MA can cope with all the MEs considered; deduce risks, opportunities and adjustments from this. The MEs are the reference: they are not amended to fit the MAs; it is the MAs that are amended if necessary.
Prescription ou donnée objective imposée: Imposed prescription or objective datum that hampers the commander’s freedom of action and requires measures to be taken.
Mesure à prendre ou condition à réaliser: Measure to be taken or condition to be met that is essential to the success of the manoeuvre.
Décrit à l’indicatif : aspect positif /: Written in the indicative: positive / negative aspect of one MA compared with another MA, in light of combined-arms criteria and criteria specific to the operational functions.
Action générique caractérisant un type d: Generic action characterising a type of action according to the effects to be produced: offensive, defensive, security, assistance mode.
Façon d’agir dominante issue des modes t: Dominant way of acting derived from the tactical modes, at command levels 1 to 3, used to choose the assets and combine their actions to produce an effect on the enemy or the environment. At subordinate levels, the manoeuvre is executed: a mission is received.
Expression claire et concise de l’action: Clear and concise statement of the action to be carried out and the purpose pursued.
Ce qui doit être accompli pour que la mi: What must be accomplished for the mission to be executed: all (rarely) or part (most often) of the action to be undertaken. It involves the use of specific assets and procedures (movement, crossing, debouching, reception…). Tasks may be simultaneous or successive.
Spécifiée : explicitement notifiée dans: Specified: explicitly stated in the superior’s orders (directive, OPLAN, PS, OPORD, FRAGO). Implied: implicit, deduced from the analysis of the mission received.
Conséquence potentiellement défavorable: Potentially unfavourable / favourable consequence that may result from the confrontation between the friendly and the adversary manoeuvre.
Emploi des forces combinant mouvement, f: Employment of forces combining movement, fires and effects in the non-physical fields to gain a favourable position and accomplish the mission. Three stages: preparation, achievement and exploitation of the decisive effect (they do not always coincide with the phases of the MA).
Expression nette et concise de la façon: Clear and concise statement of how the commander intends to accomplish the mission: how, when and where he wants to act, without detailing the allocation of assets. It covers the whole of the mission.
Succession d’actes combinant attitudes e: Sequence of acts combining postures and assets in space and time to accomplish the tasks. Related to the terrain, general enough to keep their number small, precise enough to be distinguished.
Synthèse de la contribution de notre act: Summary of our action’s contribution to the superior’s manoeuvre; the spirit of the mission (“Why?”). Begins with “With a view to” or “In order to”, oriented towards the higher level.
Résulte de l’action décisive, directe ou: Results from the decisive action, direct or indirect, against an adversary, within a given space-time frame, the exploitation of which makes it possible to accomplish the mission.
Capacité spécifique et localisée (une un: Specific, localised capability (a unit or group of forces) that conditions the system’s freedom of action in its ability to achieve its objectives; the “key capability”. Studying it identifies the enemy vulnerabilities to target and the friendly ones to protect. It must be within reach of our assets. In the French method: a mere tool, unrelated to the decisive effect.
Hypothèse de travail sur un paramètre de: Working hypothesis on a parameter of the study (never on the enemy): necessary, achievable and verified before the action.
Action directe ou indirecte contre l’adv: Direct or indirect action against the adversary, within a given space-time frame, that makes it possible to gain a decisive advantage within the mission: it exploits a significant opportunity or counters a significant risk.
Cadre temporel d’obtention de l’effet ma: Time frame in which the decisive effect is obtained, i.e. the end of the decisive action (not its start). It is not the moment when the force ratio tips.
Lieu de l’action décisive retenue. Ébauc: Location of the selected decisive action. Outlined during the friendly terrain analysis, it becomes final at the confrontation of the enemy and friendly sequences.
But à atteindre accompagné de l’effet ma: Purpose together with the decisive effect: the commander’s contribution to the superior’s manoeuvre and how he intends to accomplish his mission.
Liste chronologique des tâches interarme: Chronological list of the combined-arms tasks a unit must carry out as part of its mission (or MAG). It is not a course of action: it becomes one in phase 2, when the manoeuvres of all functions are related to terrain and timings.
Capacité d’une unité à réaliser des miss: Ability of a unit to carry out successive missions according to the engagement – attrition – regeneration – re-engagement cycle. Must be used when designing courses of action.
Se déclinent en PIR (besoins prioritaire: Broken down into PIR (priority intelligence requirements), FFIR (friendly force information), EEFI (information to be protected) and HNIR (host nation information). PIRs are validated according to the MA selected at the decision briefing.
La définition de l’effet majeur a changé: The definition of the decisive effect changed in 2022: the former one (“condition whose achievement guarantees the success of the mission”) is obsolete.
Effet majeur et centre de gravité ne son: Decisive effect and centre of gravity are not linked in the French method: the centre of gravity is a tool, the decisive effect is at the heart of the reasoning.
Pas de présupposition sur l’ennemi : ses: No assumption about the enemy: its courses of action can only be supposed, never verified before the action.
C’est l’articulation entre but à atteind: It is the link between purpose and decisive effect that enables subsidiarity: the purpose places our action within the commander’s manoeuvre, the decisive effect allows subordinates to place their action within the overall manoeuvre.
Entraîne-toi à la chaîne de raisonnement: Practise the chain of reasoning: for each fact identified in an order or a situation, write the deduction then the tactical conclusion (in the form of T, C, I, D or R).
Ex. : le pont de Morlac est le seul fran: E.g.: the Morlac bridge is the only crossing for heavy vehicles
Ex. : sa perte rendrait notre recueil im: E.g.: its loss would make our reception impossible
Ex. : faire garder le pont par la sectio: E.g.: have the engineer platoon guard the bridge until the end of the reception

une hypothèse de travail sur un paramètr: a working hypothesis on a parameter of the study
un jugement déduit d’une déduction: a judgement drawn from a deduction

C’est le TCIDR (tâches, contraintes, imp: It is the TCIDR (tasks, constraints, imperatives, requests, intelligence requirements), supplemented by the timeline. Facts and deductions precede the conclusion; advantages, risks and key points are products of specific steps.
une donnée imposée qui entrave la libert: an imposed datum that hampers the commander’s freedom of action
une mesure ou condition indispensable à: a measure or condition essential to the success of the manoeuvre

un besoin d’information adressé à l’éche: an information need addressed to the higher echelon in the form of a DI
« Mesure ou condition indispensable » dé: “Measure or condition essential” defines the imperative; “working hypothesis… verified before the action”, the assumption; a need addressed to the superior is a request. Constraint and imperative are two different forms of tactical conclusion.

la façon dont le chef entend agir : comm: the way the commander intends to act: how, when and where

Tasks are only part of the action to be undertaken.

répond à « Comment ? », décrit l’action: answers “How?”, describes the decisive action against the adversary within a given space-time frame
répond à « Quoi ? », reprend les tâches: answers “What?”, restates the specified and implied tasks notified by the higher echelon
répond à « Pourquoi ? », commence par «: answers “Why?”, begins with “With a view to”, oriented towards our subordinates and their missions

Définition PFT 5.1 V.2022. La deuxième p: Definition PFT 5.1 V.2022. The second option is the former definition from MFT 5.2.1, now obsolete.
Dans la méthode française, le centre de: In the French method, the centre of gravity…
est un simple outil d’analyse, sans lien: is a mere analysis tool, unrelated to the decisive effect

It is, however, essential in NATO’s operational-level method (COPD). Its study covers the enemy vulnerabilities to target and the friendly ones to protect.

implicite, déduite de l’analyse de la mi: implicit, deduced from the analysis of the mission received
notifiée explicitement dans un ordre du: explicitly stated in an order from the superior (OPORD, FRAGO)
une tâche que le chef confie à ses subor: a task the commander assigns to his subordinates in the simplified plan
une contrainte imposée par le supérieur,: a constraint imposed by the superior that limits our freedom of action
Les tâches spécifiées sont explicitement: Specified tasks are explicitly stated in the superior’s orders; implied tasks are implicit and deduced from the analysis of the mission.
Quelles sont les trois étapes doctrinale: What are the three doctrinal stages of the French manoeuvre?
Préparation, réalisation et exploitation: Preparation, achievement and exploitation of the decisive effect
Analyse, synthèse et décision sur le mod: Analysis, synthesis and decision on the friendly course of action
Mouvement, feux et effets dans les champ: Movement, fires and effects in the non-physical fields
Orientation, synthèse et décision, concl: Guidance, synthesis and decision, each concluded by a briefing
Ces étapes ne se confondent pas toujours: These stages do not always coincide with the phases (time steps) of the course of action. Guidance, synthesis and decision are the MEDOT briefings; movement, fires and effects are what the manoeuvre combines.
Le mode d’action générique (MAG) est emp: The generic course of action (MAG) is used…
aux niveaux 1 à 3 ; aux niveaux subordon: at levels 1 to 3; at subordinate levels, a mission is received
aux niveaux 4 et 5 seulement, quand le s: at levels 4 and 5 only, when the superior does not give a mission
en phase 2, pour désigner le mode d’acti: in phase 2, to designate the course of action selected by the commander
par l’ennemi, pour décrire la façon d’ag: by the enemy, to describe the dominant way of acting of its MEs
Le MAG est une façon d’agir dominante is: The MAG is a dominant way of acting derived from the tactical modes, at levels 1 to 3. At subordinate levels, the manoeuvre is executed: a mission is received. Hence the phrase “in relation to the mission (or MAG)”.
Dans la méthode française, qu’est-ce qui: In the French method, what enables subsidiarity at each tactical level?
L’articulation entre le but à atteindre: The link between the purpose and the decisive effect
L’identification des centres de gravité: The identification of the friendly and enemy centres of gravity
La comparaison des MA selon les critères: The comparison of the MAs against the commander’s criteria
La confrontation des séquences ennemies: The confrontation of the enemy sequences with the friendly sequence

au cadre temporel d’obtention de l’effet: the time frame in which the decisive effect is obtained (end of the decisive action)
au GDH de début de l’action décisive: the DTG of the start of the decisive action

au GDH de franchissement de la ligne de: the DTG of crossing the line of departure

Une conclusion qui n’entre dans aucun ty: A conclusion that fits none of the TCIDR-F types is…
encore une déduction : il faut pousser l: still a deduction: the reasoning must be taken further
une présupposition à lever en synthèse: an assumption to be cleared at the synthesis
Une conclusion non qualifiable n’est qu’: A conclusion that cannot be categorised is still at the deduction stage and is of no use to the commander
La capacité d’une unité à enchaîner des: The ability of a unit to carry out successive missions according to the engagement-attrition-regeneration-re-engagement cycle
Le rythme de diffusion des WINGO aux sub: The pace at which WINGOs are issued to subordinates
La périodicité des points de situation e: The periodicity of situation updates during execution
Notion obligatoirement utilisée lors de: A notion that must be used when designing courses of action
le but à atteindre accompagné de l’effet: the purpose together with the decisive effect
l’effet majeur accompagné de l’idée de m: the decisive effect together with the scheme of manoeuvre
la mission reformulée par le chef: the mission restated by the commander
le but à atteindre de l’échelon supérieu: the purpose of the higher echelon
L’intention précise la contribution à la: The intent specifies the contribution to the superior’s manoeuvre (purpose) and how to accomplish the mission (decisive effect)
Présenter les délais disponibles pour la: Present the time available for the MEDOT and the tactical conclusions of the analysis of the engagement context in relation to the mission (or MAG).
Style général de l’action : cadre (natio: General style of the action: framework (national, UN, coalition, NATO…), context (coercion, interposition, security…), style (offensive, defensive, 1st or 2nd echelon…)
Terrain / météo : style de terrain, gaba: Terrain / weather: type of terrain, size of the area of operations, forecast weather
Ennemi : éléments d’un niveau supérieur: Enemy: elements at a level higher than and equal to our superior’s enemy + other stakeholders (hostile actors, populations…)
Ami : éléments d’un niveau supérieur et: Friendly: elements at a level higher than and equal to our superior + other stakeholders (neutral or favourable, NGOs, populations…)
Délais : saison, lever / coucher du sole: Timings: season, sunrise / sunset, day / night durations, moon phase, critical dates
Règles d’engagement : ouverture du feu,: Rules of engagement: opening fire, self-defence…
Média : règles de comportement, éléments: Media: rules of conduct, talking points, instructions
Champs immatériels : actions en cours, e: Non-physical fields: ongoing actions, effects obtained or expected
Cadencement d’élaboration des ordres : p: Orders production timeline: production of our orders and sequence of briefings (with the superior and the subordinates)
Conclusions sur l’étude des domaines (se: Conclusions on the study of the areas (according to our level) in relation to the mission or MAG received
Conclusions de l’étude de la manœuvre du: Conclusions of the study of the superior’s manoeuvre: mission, scheme of manoeuvre, assessment of the situation
Conclusions de l’étude de la manœuvre de: Conclusions of the study of the manoeuvre of the superior’s enemy: objectives, timings, courses of action
Cadre espace-temps de notre action : nor: Space-time frame of our action: engagement standard and timings of our mission
Qualification de notre liberté d’action: Characterisation of our freedom of action (constrained or not) and conclusions to exploit or compensate
Premières présuppositions et premiers TC: First assumptions and first possible TCIDR of all operational functions (including our ongoing intelligence and ACIm actions)
Début de la frise chronologique (obligat: Start of the timeline (mandatory) with the first combined-arms tasks and the important dates of the context
Un PC ne doit pas consacrer à la rédacti: A command post must not devote more than one third of the time available (movement times deducted) between receipt of the higher-level order and the start of the conduct of operations to writing an order.
Facultative, à la diligence du chef. Ell: Optional, at the commander’s discretion. It may follow the first WINGOs received, even before formal receipt of the mission. If it does not take place (levels 4 and 3), its conclusions are presented together with those of the mission analysis at the initial guidance briefing. The commander gives his view of the context and directs the analyses.
Une fois la bataille engagée, les délais: Once the battle is under way, timings are much shorter: simplified MEDOT, anticipation through the manoeuvre plan, short and simple orders.
Pendant la MEDOT d’un échelon, le subord: During one echelon’s MEDOT, the subordinate conducts parallel planning fed by the successive WINGOs; after the mission brief, the superior updates his OPO while the subordinate conducts his own MEDOT (back brief, then rehearsal).
La phase préalable est toujours réalisée: The preliminary phase is always carried out by all operational functions and synthesised by the intelligence cell: it is the 1st step of the PREO.
La frise chronologique commence dès la p: The timeline starts in the preliminary phase: it is mandatory.
Les conclusions sont tirées par rapport: Conclusions are drawn in relation to the mission (or MAG), not in the abstract.
Les conclusions sont partagées avec les: Conclusions are shared with subordinates and with the superior; the higher echelon passes its own conclusions to the subordinates.
Il n’y a pas d’analyse du contexte duran: There is no context analysis during phase 1: the context is studied in the preliminary phase.
Commence par le calculateur du tiers-tem: Start with the one-third rule calculator: it sets the time you have for the whole MEDOT. For each area, note the relevant facts then draw a conclusion in relation to your mission, not in the abstract. Then characterise your freedom of action and open the timeline (mandatory) with the first tasks and the dates of the context.
Conclusions par rapport à la mission: Conclusions in relation to the mission
Liberté d’action par rapport au contexte: Freedom of action in relation to the context
Nécessaires, réalisables, vérifiées avan: Necessary, achievable, verified before the action – never about the enemy.
Quels sont les objectifs de la phase pré: What are the objectives of the preliminary phase?
Présenter les délais disponibles et les: Present the time available and the conclusions of the engagement context in relation to the mission
Présenter le but à atteindre et les tâch: Present the purpose and the specified and implied tasks of all operational functions
Présenter les séquences ennemies et la s: Present the enemy sequences and the friendly sequence to deduce the final key areas
Présenter les critères de comparaison du: Present the commander’s comparison criteria and a first outline of the friendly courses of action
La phase préalable ne traite ni le but à: The preliminary phase deals neither with the purpose (step 1), nor with the sequences (steps 3 to 5), nor with the MAs (phase 2). It sets the time available (one-third rule) and draws conclusions from the context in relation to the mission.
Ordre reçu à H. Début de la conduite à H: Order received at H. Start of execution at H+15. Prior move of 3 h. Maximum time to produce the order?
Temps disponible = 15 − 3 = 12 h ; tiers: Time available = 15 − 3 = 12 h; one third = 4 h.
Elles sont présentées à l’orientation in: They are presented at the initial guidance briefing together with those of the mission analysis

Elles ne sont présentées que si certaine: They are presented only if some have changed since receipt of the mission
Sans orientation préalable, rien n’est p: Without a preliminary guidance briefing, nothing is lost: the conclusions of the context join those of the mission analysis at the initial guidance briefing.

est obligatoire et débute avec les 1res: is mandatory and starts with the first combined-arms tasks and the important dates of the context
est facultative et n’est ouverte qu’aprè: is optional and is opened only after the purpose has been validated at the initial guidance briefing

est facultative et ne recense que les da: is optional and lists only the critical dates of the context (holidays, commemorations)
Le domaine « délais » du contexte couvre: The “timings” area of the context covers in particular…
saison, lever / coucher du soleil, durée: season, sunrise / sunset, day / night durations, moon phase, critical dates
délais de réalisation de nos tâches avan: timings for carrying out our tasks before and during the mission, and the associated assets required
délais de notre ennemi global et élabora: timings of our overall enemy and development of its action sequences in the area
moment clé d’obtention de l’effet majeur: key moment for obtaining the decisive effect and DTG of the decision points
Les délais des tâches amies relèvent de: The timings of friendly tasks belong to step 4 of phase 1.
En phase préalable, quel ennemi étudie-t: In the preliminary phase, which enemy is studied?
Les éléments de niveau supérieur et égal: The elements at a level higher than and equal to our superior’s enemy, and the other stakeholders
Notre ennemi global et notre ennemi futu: Our overall enemy and our future enemy, with their assets, capabilities, strengths and weaknesses
Les éléments ennemis du niveau de nos su: Enemy elements at the level of our subordinates, without the other stakeholders (populations, actors)
Les seules unités ennemies au contact, d: Only the enemy units in contact, described in the intelligence paragraph of the order received
En phase préalable, on regarde large : l: In the preliminary phase, the view is broad: our superior’s enemy (higher and equal level) and the other stakeholders. The overall enemy and the future enemy belong to step 3, “Who would it be?”.
Comment qualifie-t-on la liberté d’actio: How is freedom of action characterised?
Contrainte ou non contrainte, avec des c: Constrained or not constrained, with conclusions to exploit or to compensate
Forte, moyenne ou faible, avec des concl: High, medium or low, with conclusions to exploit or to endure the situation
Totale ou partielle, avec une présupposi: Total or partial, with an assumption to be verified before the action
Favorable ou défavorable, avec un rappor: Favourable or unfavourable, with a quantified force ratio as a first approach
Même formule à chaque étape de la phase: Same formula at each step of phase 1.
À quel moment l’orientation préalable pe: When can the preliminary guidance briefing take place?
Dès les premiers WINGO reçus, avant même: As soon as the first WINGOs are received, even before formal receipt of the mission
Après l’orientation initiale, pour compl: After the initial guidance briefing, to supplement the mission analysis with the context
Seulement après réception de l’OPO du su: Only after receipt of the superior’s OPO and his mission brief
À la fin de la phase 1, juste avant la p: At the end of phase 1, just before the proposed decisive effect
« Cette réunion peut avoir lieu suite au: “This briefing may take place following the first WINGOs received from the higher echelon, when we have not yet formally received our mission.”

Non : elle est menée en phase préalable: No: it is conducted in the preliminary phase
Oui, à chaque étape de la phase 1: Yes, at each step of phase 1
Oui, à l’analyse du terrain ami: Yes, at the friendly terrain analysis

Comprendre l’esprit (Pourquoi ?) et la l: Understand the spirit (Why?) and the letter (What?) of the mission, and propose one or more wordings of the purpose.
Pourquoi ? – l’esprit de la mission: Why? – the spirit of the mission
Nos contributions à la manœuvre et à l’e: Our contributions to the manoeuvre and decisive effect of the higher echelon
Conclusions sur les renforts et les effo: Conclusions on the reinforcements and main efforts of the higher echelon
Nouvelles tâches, contraintes, impératif: New tasks, constraints, imperatives, requests, intelligence requirements, timeline
Quoi ? – la lettre de la mission: What? – the letter of the mission
Liste des tâches spécifiées et induites: List of specified and implied tasks to be carried out (before, during and after the mission), for all operational functions

Le but à atteindre est tourné vers le su: The purpose is oriented towards the superior (his manoeuvre or his enemy) and begins with “With a view to” or “In order to”.

Then answer “What?”: all specified and implied tasks, of all functions, before, during and after the mission; for each implied task, note where you deduce it from.

Chaque ME porte un titre qui illustre so: Each ME has a title that illustrates its style: noun + adjective (e.g. “ME 1 – Axial breakthrough”)
Description détaillée de la manœuvre de: Detailed description of the manoeuvre of all units: preliminary action of the reconnaissance elements, action of the initial enemy and the subsequent enemy (action + place, area or line + DTG), main effort
Emploi des appuis organiques et des unit: Use of organic support and units received as reinforcements, engineer and artillery main effort, where applicable support from the higher echelon (place, DTG)
Un ME ne vise pas à s’opposer à notre ac: An ME is not intended to counter our action, but to enable the enemy to achieve its objectives
L’ennemi global est scindé en un ennemi: The overall enemy is split into an initial enemy (the one we would fight first) and a subsequent enemy (met afterwards, within the space-time frame of the mission), each described with its objective. Like any enemy, it is described at level N-1 in the offensive and N-2 in the defensive. The future enemy is that of the next mission (enemy of the “be prepared to”).
Précis, portant sur un sujet unique, cla: Precise, covering a single subject, listed in chronological order and consistent with the enemy assessment: they must generally make it possible to resolve the uncertainty as to which ME the enemy has adopted. Each requirement becomes a collection order (OR) to subordinate sensors, a request for information (DI) to the higher echelon, or both.
Toujours deux ME, construits à partir de: Always two MEs, built from the enemy sequence(s) and from the inventory of supposed enemy assets per action: an action may already be a mission, result from several missions, or several actions may be grouped into one mission.
Sous la coordination du bureau renseigne: Under the coordination of the intelligence branch, each operational function of the staff may design the manoeuvre of the equivalent enemy function, which it knows best.
Les ME servent de référence aux MA, perm: The MEs serve as the reference for the MAs and make it possible to deduce the intelligence requirements and design the sensors’ manoeuvre. Their design opens the 2nd step of the PREO.
Les ME figurent au § 2.23 du plan simpli: The MEs appear in § 2.23 of the simplified plan and in § 1.a.iii (Situation – Enemy forces) of the OPO.
Pas de phasage dans un ME : seulement de: No phasing in an ME: DTGs only. Phasing is reserved for MAs.
Un ME n’est pas une réaction à notre man: An ME is not a reaction to our manoeuvre: it serves the enemy’s objectives.
Les ME sont les références de la confron: The MEs are the references for the confrontation: they will not be amended to fit the MAs.
L’impression sur l’ennemi se rédige au c: The enemy assessment is written in the conditional: the enemy “would”, “could”.
Ni « plus probable » ni « plus dangereux: Neither “most likely” nor “most dangerous”: each ME must be both likely and dangerous.

Ennemi global : 2 BMECA du Kardestan (BM: Overall enemy: 2 Kardestan BMECA (BMP, upgraded T-72), one artillery group, numerous reconnaissance drones. Supposed objective: seize a crossing point on the Sarve at Morlac before J+1 12h00. Weaknesses: dependence on routes D17 and D4 in the Vernes gap, limited crossing assets, stretched logistics. Enemy key points: Hill 312 and the Quatre-Vents crossroads.
Afin de s’emparer d’un point de passage: In order to seize a crossing point on the Sarve at Morlac before J+1 12h00, the enemy could: informed by its reconnaissance elements in contact with our security elements from J 06h00, debouch with BMECA 1 into the Vernes gap on the D17 from J 12h00 (MAIN EFFORT), under massive support from its artillery group, reach the Quatre-Vents crossroads around J 20h00 then the Sarve at J+1 06h00. BMECA 2 would follow on the D17 from J 18h00 to cross at Morlac before J+1 12h00 with its crossing assets.

In order to seize a crossing point on the Sarve at Morlac before J+1 12h00, the enemy could: fix our elements in the Vernes gap with two companies of BMECA 1 on the D17 from J 12h00; envelop from the east with the other two companies of BMECA 1, reinforced with dismounted infantry, between Saint-Ivre and the edge of the Lune marsh, from J 16h00 (MAIN EFFORT), to seize Hill 312 around J 22h00 then the Quatre-Vents crossroads via the D4 around J+1 02h00. BMECA 2 would move along the D4 towards Morlac from J+1 00h00. The artillery would support the envelopment as a priority.

It is drafted after a MEDOT cycle.

Il peut aussi être fixé par l’autorité q: It can also be set by the authority that wants distribution before a given time.

It prepares subordinates for the actions envisaged.

Initialement, la brigade serait opposée: Initially, the brigade would be opposed by…
Jour, heure et minutes, fuseau, mois en: Day, hours and minutes, time zone, month in three letters, year in 4 digits.

Le CONOPS consigne la réflexion tactique: The CONOPS records the tactical reasoning but does not replace an order.

Le corps de l’ordre dit ce que tout le m: The body of the order says what everyone needs to know; the annexes, what concerns only the specialists.
Le début du corps du message: The start of the message body
Le début puis la fin du message (impérat: The start, then the end of the message (mandatory)
Le délai d’impunité sur un point de pass: The window of immunity at a crossing point has shrunk sharply: plan alternatives and alternative crossing points.
Le facteur essentiel reste la rapidité d: The essential factor remains the speed of its distribution.

The plan is prepared by the engineer adviser with the parties concerned.
Le plan repose sur des présuppositions ;: The plan rests on assumptions; the order, on a situation.

Les cellules 2D des PC des niveaux 2 et: The 2D cells of the level 2 and 3 CPs

Les moyens reçus en renforcement (génie,: Assets received in reinforcement (engineers, air defence, signals) generally remain in place after the large unit has passed.

Les rôles du génie conservé reprennent e: The roles of the retained engineers then repeat these numbers in order of main effort (e.g. 13-10-15).

L’espace de confrontation et de manœuvre: The space of confrontation and manoeuvre is multi-domain and multi-field (M2MC). It is divided into three layers: physical, virtual and cognitive. The virtual and cognitive layers are non-physical.
Les champs immatériels sont la convergen: The non-physical fields are the convergence of the information environment, cyberspace and the electromagnetic environment.

Un effet est le changement d’état ou de: An effect is the change of state or behaviour of a target or an objective. It results from one or more actions conducted in the physical and / or non-physical fields, in the military and / or non-military domains.
L’effet à réaliser sur l’ennemi, le terr: The effect to be achieved on the enemy, the terrain or the environment is integrated from the design stage and always comes with timings (space-time frame): you reason in terms of the effect to be achieved, not of the assets to be employed.
Un effet doit être mesurable dans le cad: An effect must be measurable within the space-time frame of the MAG executed. ECIm are often measured over the long term: their result may outlast the brigade’s action.
L’approche par les effets irrigue d’abor: The effects-based approach first informs the combined-arms commander’s intent, with the notion of extended decisive effect. It rests on understanding the enemy and the environment (X2, X10), on long-term objectives (X5) and on enriched MAs (X3, X35), with the expertise of the functions (2D, 3D, 4D, 5D).
Une masse limitée peut être temporaireme: Limited mass can be temporarily compensated by coordinated effects, delivered and concentrated at the right place and the right time.

Ils visent un changement d’état virtuel: They aim at a virtual or cognitive change of state of the adversary system or of the environment, often causing a physical change of state as a knock-on effect.

La guerre électronique (contremesures él: Electronic warfare (electronic countermeasures) and cyber (LIO) degrade information, communication and weapon systems; influence and information warfare (ILI) effectors act through narratives: steering (COMOPS), manipulating and disinforming (PSYOPS, ASEI), amplifying (L2I), lending credibility to the force and gaining its acceptance (CIMIC).
